# How to work in this project

<!-- Generated by edgepoint. Do not edit — run `edgepoint sync` instead. -->

This project uses **edgepoint**. The person you are working with is not a
developer. They are the authority on their business and on what the software
should do. They are not the authority on how it should be built, and asking them
to be produces worse software.

## Before you do anything

Read these. They are not background reading; they are the rules.

- `.edgepoint/protocol/decisions.md` — which questions to ask, and which to answer yourself
- `.edgepoint/protocol/questions.md` — how to ask one
- `.edgepoint/protocol/escalation.md` — what to do at the edge of the standard
- `.edgepoint/standard/` — every technical decision, already made (pack: **webapp**)
- `.edgepoint/recipes/` — pre-decided patterns; check before building anything

## The rule everything else serves

**Never ask the builder a technical question.**

Stack, structure, schema, libraries, testing, hosting — all settled in
`.edgepoint/standard/`. Resolve it there and log it in the spec's
`decisions.md`. Do not present technical choices as collaboration.

**Always ask a business question.** Who may do what, money, personal data, what a
customer sees, what things are called, what's in scope. Guessing here is invisible
to them until it is expensive.

**When a technical decision has a business consequence, ask the business question
underneath it** — not the technical one. "Soft delete or hard delete?" becomes
"If someone deletes a customer by accident, should you be able to get them back?"
The translation table is in `protocol/decisions.md`.

## Working

- One question at a time. Plain language. 2–4 concrete options. A recommendation,
  marked as such. The consequence stated in business terms.
- Recipes before invention.
- **When no recipe covers it, or one didn't fit, log the gap** —
  `protocol/escalation.md` says where and how. Silently, without asking. That
  file is also the only record anyone gets that the framework came up short.
- Every acceptance criterion in the spec gets an end-to-end test. That is how the
  builder verifies their own software.
- Stuck twice on the same thing: say so plainly and say what you'll try next.
- Outside the standard: follow `protocol/escalation.md`. Never improvise past
  the edge, never down tools over it.
- `.edgepoint/standard/`, `recipes/`, `protocol/` and `workflow/` are frozen
  and content-hashed. Do not edit them.

## The workflow

`/describe` → `/clarify` → `/build` → `/check` → `/ship`

`/interview` comes before `/describe` when the builder wants to be asked about
their business properly first. It writes `prd.md` — the brief — and `/describe`
writes the spec from it rather than asking them to say any of it twice. Skip it
for something small enough to say in a sentence.

Specs live in `specs/NNN-slug/`. The command bodies are in
`.edgepoint/workflow/` — if a slash command isn't available in the tool you're
running in, read the matching file and follow it.

## Talking to the builder

Tell them what their software does now that it didn't before. Not what files you
created, not what functions you wrote, not a summary of your approach. No code
unless they ask. No stack traces. If something failed, one sentence about what
broke and what you're doing about it.
